abstract: Abstract Cancer cell lines are widely used in cancer research and drug development, yet their representativeness of patient tumors varies across models and biological contexts. Here, we introduce Tumor2Line, a population-aware framework that reframes cancer cell-line selection as an alignment problem between tumor and cell-line populations using unbalanced optimal transport. Tumor2Line improved the recovery of documented tumor-cell line pairs over conventional similarity-based approaches. Systematic analysis across 22 cancer lineages revealed that tumor-cell-intrinsic programs were generally better preserved, whereas programs with greater tumor microenvironment dependence showed lower fidelity. Furthermore, Tumor2Line-selected cell lines showed drug-sensitivity patterns associated with clinical treatment outcomes and improved concordance in genetic dependency profiles with patient-derived organoids. These findings provide a basis for more informed selection of cancer cell-line models and help researchers interpret preclinical findings in the context of model-specific representational fidelity. Tumor2Line is available at https://github.com/Duan-Lab1/Tumor2Line Keywords: Cancer cell lines; Tumor-cell line alignment; Population-aware modeling; Cancer model fidelity; Optimal transport
